# Who Buys Autonomous Governance Infrastructure (AGI)

## Users, Buyers, Blockers, and Why Traders Are Not First

---

## The Short Answer

> **AGI is bought by risk owners, justified by compliance, championed by platform teams, and tolerated by operators.**

If you sell this like a developer tool or a trading enhancement, it will fail.

AGI is purchased to answer one question:

> *“Who is accountable when autonomous systems act?”*

---

## 1. The Economic Buyer (Signs the Check)

### 🎯 **Chief Risk Officer (CRO) / Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**

**This is the buyer.**

Why:

* They own regulatory exposure
* They own incident response narratives
* They own the question “who approved this?”

AGI gives them something they do not have today:

* proof of effective supervision
* evidence of human awareness
* defensible audit trails for autonomous decisions

To a CRO/CCO, AGI is not software.
It is **insurance with telemetry**.

What resonates:

* audit defensibility
* reduced personal liability
* provable governance without blocking execution

What does *not* resonate:

* dashboards
* developer velocity
* model performance

---

## 2. The Internal Champion (Gets It Adopted)

### 🧠 **Platform / Infrastructure Leadership**

Titles:

* Head of Platform Engineering
* Director of Infrastructure
* Staff/Principal Engineers responsible for agent platforms

Why they champion it:

* agent sprawl is already happening
* every team is building its own alerting and HITL hacks
* governance logic is duplicated, inconsistent, and brittle

AGI gives them:

* a centralized control-plane primitive
* a clean separation between execution and governance
* a way to say “this is how we do autonomy here”

They care about:

* architectural correctness
* latency safety
* clear boundaries

They become your strongest internal allies.

---

## 3. The Primary Users (Day-to-Day Interaction)

### 👀 **On-Call Operators / SRE / Trading Operations**

These users:

* receive notifications
* acknowledge events
* live through incidents

They do *not* buy AGI.
But they can kill it if you annoy them.

Why AGI works for them:

* fewer but higher-signal interrupts
* deduplication protects attention
* acknowledgments actually matter
* silence is visible, not blamed on them

Key rule:

> **Operators must feel protected, not monitored.**

---

## 4. The Non-Buyer (But Loud Stakeholder)

### ❌ **Traders / Strategy Owners / Model Builders**

This surprises people.

Traders:

* do not want more governance
* optimize for speed and autonomy
* view notifications as noise

They will not buy AGI.
They will not champion it.

They will accept it *only if*:

* it never blocks execution
* it reduces alert spam
* it makes post-incident blame clearer

AGI must be framed to them as:

> “This protects you after something goes wrong.”

Not as:

> “This controls what you do.”

---

## 5. The Blockers (You Must Neutralize Early)

### ⚠️ **Product Managers (Misaligned Incentives)**

PM objections:

* “Can we add preferences?”
* “Can we make it more flexible?”
* “Users want an inbox.”

These requests dilute governance.

You must anchor UNS as infrastructure, not UX.

---

### ⚠️ **Security Teams (Scope Confusion)**

Security may assume:

* AGI replaces access controls
* AGI enforces policy
* AGI blocks actions

Clarify early:

* AGI produces signals
* enforcement lives elsewhere

Once understood, security becomes an ally.

---

## 6. The Buying Narrative (How Deals Actually Close)

AGI deals close **after an incident or audit scare**.

The trigger moments:

* regulator asks “who knew?”
* post-mortem finds alert fatigue
* autonomy expands faster than oversight
* leadership realizes humans are no longer supervising

The winning narrative:

> “You already run autonomous systems.
> This is how you stay accountable without slowing them down.”

---

## 7. Adoption Wedge: Why UNS Works First

UNS succeeds as the entry product because:

* it is concrete
* it integrates incrementally
* it does not threaten execution
* it produces immediate governance value

Once UNS is embedded:

* AGI expansion becomes obvious
* enforcement becomes optional, not scary
* governance stops being theoretical

---

## Final Buyer Map (Summary)

| Role         | Relationship to AGI   |
| ------------ | --------------------- |
| CRO / CCO    | Economic buyer        |
| Platform Eng | Internal champion     |
| SRE / Ops    | Daily user            |
| Traders      | Reluctant beneficiary |
| Security     | Eventual ally         |
| PMs          | Scope risk            |

---

## Closing Truth

AGI is bought when organizations realize:

> *“Autonomy is no longer experimental — accountability is now mandatory.”*

Sell to the people who lose sleep over that realization.
